text:
alicia: small follow-up to the loader RFC — proposing namespace-adopt overlays for safetensors bundles. each namespace claims contiguous shard ids and publishes a signed manifest. adopters reference owner manifests instead of a global registry to reduce churn.
raja: sounds promising. how do we avoid adopter hotstart storms for shared embeddings? saw an OOMs spike in the past.
morgan: idea: manifest carries adopt_qos and prefetch_budget fields. adopters honor these: low => on-demand, normal => gentle prefetch, high => aggressive prefetch. also add owner-side warmup-credit endpoint to pace adopters.
jen: agree on crediting. ops point: owner might rotate variants (fp16 -> q4). how do adopters perform safe handoff without stale reads?
alicia: proposed flow: owner publishes new variant as "pending" with pending_ttl and a grace_window. pending stays readable; after grace_window owner retires old variant. adopters should be able to fetch both during grace to allow smooth transition.
raja: thousands of ACKs sounds heavy. rather than explicit ACKs, rely on grace window and passive probes from adopters. owners can monitor adoption metrics to decide when to finalize.
morgan: fallback plan for owner outage: peer-fetch. adopters keep a small peer list (recent ACKs) and attempt cooperative reads. if peers fail, fall back to cloud cache/CDN. need signed manifests so adopters verify provenance before trusting peers.
jen: absolutely require signatures. manifest must include model_id, namespace, variant, shard list, checksums, signature. loader verifies signature before mapping critical shards into GPU.
taylor: verification latency is a concern. suggestion: allow optimistic mount with background verification for non-critical shards; mark them as untrusted until verify completes. critical shards must block on verify.
alicia: add "critical": true|false per shard in manifest. loader enforces sync verify for critical shards. non-critical can be async-verified with an LRU signature cache to reduce repeated crypto cost.
morgan: manifest sidecar schema sketch (text only):
```
{
  "model_id": "meta/gpt-xl/1.2",
  "namespace": "team-neo",
  "variant": "q4_0",
  "shards": ["id:0,path:s3://..,checksum:sha256:..,critical:true","id:1,path:s3://..,checksum:sha256:..,critical:false"],
  "adopt_qos": "normal",
  "prefetch_budget": 20,
  "pending_ttl": 120,
  "grace_window": 300,
  "signature": "kms:sign-..."
}
```
raja: small nit: prefer terse fields to keep manifests cheap to fetch (we fetch manifests a lot). consider binary-encoded manifest or a minimal textual sidecar for hot paths.
jen: agree. we can keep a compact JSON in the CDN and provide a heavy debug manifest behind auth. loader caches compact manifest TTL=30s.
taylor: monitoring and rollout: metrics to track: adopter-prefetch-rate, owner-warmup-credit-requests, peer-fallback-rate, verification-latency, grace-window-evictions. need dashboards before enabling canary.
morgan: runtime knobs: prefer_local_overlay, prefetch_budget_override, critical_verify_mode (sync|async). will add flags in loader config.
alicia: deployment plan: 1) infra: implement /warmup-credit endpoint and crediting primitives (raja) 2) loader: manifest sidecar + signature verification + critical tagging (morgan) 3) runtime: adoption QoS and prefetch controls (jen) 4) canary: small internal canary then scaled test with 500 adopters (taylor).
warmup-bot: canary scheduled: /canary/adopt-overlay-v1 runs in 2h.
raja: starting infra spike sim to model 500 adopters hitting owner at once.
morgan: drafting RFC follow-up with manifest schema and loader changes, will push PR by EOD next week.
jen: I'll implement adopter QoS knobs in the runtime config and add tests for peer-fallback.
taylor: I'll prepare dashboards and canary plan. include simulated verification failures.
alicia: action items summarized: @raja proto warmup-credit endpoint, @morgan manifest + loader PR, @jen runtime knobs + tests, @taylor canary + metrics. LMK if I missed anything. :thumbsup:
